title: The old Wolverines could not read music
summary: Bix, the piano, drums and banjo couldn't read; all by ear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well one other thing. You said that a number of the musicians could not read music.
And so, I know in your own group you had only a group of people who could. You really studied seriously since young boys. Well when you had to play with larger groups larger bands, ...
Oh yes. Yes, you had to.
Oh, I thought you said a number of them didn't read.

Well this was in the old Wolverine band. The old Wolverines. This is 1924. And the piano player couldn't read and Bix didn't read very well. Or George Johnson the tenor saxophone player didn't read very well, hardly at all, just a little bit. And the drummer didn't read. And Bob Gillette, the banjo player didn't read. But I graduated from that.

Yes, but I think that would be of some interest to other people to know just how you got people like that to work together with different instruments? Did you teach some things by rote or was it clearly an ear ...
Yes. But that's the way we learned
It turned out to be quite an accidental harmony that worked, is that it? (LAUGHTER). Harmonising I mean....
